report.title: Caveman UI/UX Audit
report.subtitle: Blind first-impression review of {{target}}
blind.what_can_i_get_or_do: What can I get or do?
methodology.body: This audit keeps two kinds of assessment apart and never merges them into one undisclosed number. Deterministic evidence comes from axe-core, Lighthouse and DOM checks that anyone can re-run and reproduce byte for byte. Probabilistic judgment comes from the blind Caveman rubric, where a fresh-context evaluator sees one viewport screenshot and nothing else, answers five first-impression questions, and scores nine weighted dimensions from 0 to 10. The two are scored separately and reported side by side; when a composite score is shown at all, its weights are printed with it. Every score formula is documented in references/rubric.md so any number here can be recomputed by hand.
limitations.body: This report is not a WCAG legal-compliance certification and not a substitute for real user research. Automated tooling catches only a fraction of accessibility barriers, and the blind rubric measures one evaluator first impression rather than the behaviour of your actual users. Lighthouse numbers move with network, machine and load, so treat them as a range rather than a verdict. Findings marked low confidence cannot fail a gate on their own. Read every finding as a hypothesis with evidence attached, and validate high-stakes decisions with real users and, where the law is involved, with a qualified accessibility auditor.
